title: VerificationLedger
description: Plugin-native verification output. Separates what the agent team produced into supported claims, challenged claims, unresolved tensions, and human-required checks. This is the core anti-sycophancy object: Argus does not promote a scaffold until the verification state is visible.

overall_status.description: verified = no critical blockers; mixed = usable with caveats; needs_revision = agent team should revise before boss/user signoff; blocked = requires human/external evidence first.

confidence.description: Confidence in the verification result, not in the business decision.

supported_claims.description: Positive validation: claims that are supported by worker evidence, code citations, source references, or cross-agent agreement.

source.description: worker_id, file path, PR ref, or external source label.

challenged_claims.description: Negative validation: claims that are unsupported, too generic, contradicted, risky, or likely to produce false confidence.

grounding.description: internal = the agents can confirm it (logic, arithmetic, code/in-repo citation, a checkable source). external = ONLY reality confirms it (market size, a regulator's actual position, a customer's actual want, performance at real scale, a third party's behavior). The agents' own cross-agreement is NOT confirmation of an external claim.

depended_on_by.description: STRUCTURAL anchors that rest on this claim — next_action ids (via their rests_on) or the literal 'current_course'. NOT sibling claims: claim-to-claim prose inference is unreliable (the model co-generated both) and is forbidden here. Non-empty => load-bearing.

root_crack.description: The GATING reality risk: the load-bearing AND external AND unconfirmed claim on a HIGH-STAKES, HARD-TO-REVERSE decision — the one that, if false, burns the user, and that no internal cross-agent agreement can validate. It blocks final_signoff/execution and seeds a decision-contract predicate (seal -> reality -> settle). NULL when no such claim exists: a reversible or low-stakes external claim is NOT a root_crack (it still ships as a non-gating armed note in human_required_checks — blocking the reversible is over-fire/mirror-clause), and an internal claim is never a risk. Being external is never a reason to withhold help — the entry must be armed (best_read + cheapest_check), never a bare 'go verify' referral.

grounding.description: Always 'external' — an internal claim is never a reality risk; the agents can just check it.

depended_on_by.description: Structural anchors (next_action ids / 'current_course') that rest on this claim — the blast radius.

why.description: One neutral line: what rests on it and why only reality can settle it.

best_read.description: Argus's best substantive answer DESPITE the uncertainty — estimate, base rate, indirect evidence, likely direction. Maximum generation: do not withhold the read just because reality has the final word.

cheapest_check.description: The armed, concrete check: WHO/WHAT confirms it, what a 'yes' looks like, and a fallback if no answer arrives. Turns a referral into help.

unresolved_tensions.description: Real disagreements that should remain visible to the user instead of being averaged away.

human_required_checks.description: Things AI cannot verify from the available repo/session context. These are immediate user/external checks, not long-term outcome grading.

claim_tests.description: Positive/negative tests the verifier applied. Useful for debugging why a claim was supported or challenged.

routing_decision.description: Next routing selected by the verify step (review). sail respects this unless the user explicitly overrides.

user_choice.description: Recorded AskUserQuestion result when the verifier had to ask the user how to handle challenged or blocked claims.
